questions.prompt: What does a data model provide for describing a database?
choices: A set of hardware instructions for reading a disk
Structure, data types, relationships, constraints, and operations on the data
A list of the current records in the database
A schedule for when individual users can access stored database files
questions.explanation: A data model supplies concepts for describing database structure, such as data types, relationships, and constraints (§2.1).

questions.prompt: Which pairings correctly distinguish data-model categories? Select all that apply.
choices: Physical models describe user-focused data and relationships
Conceptual models use concepts close to users’ view of data
Representational models are implementable while hiding storage detail
Physical models describe storage on computer media
questions.explanation: Conceptual models use user-oriented concepts, representational models bridge users and implementation, and physical models describe storage details. User-oriented entity and relationship concepts characterize conceptual models (§2.1.1).

questions.prompt: A new student record is inserted without changing the database design description. What changed, and what stayed the same?
choices: The schema and state changed because every record defines a new structure
The schema changed; the database state stayed the same
The state or extension changed; the schema or intension stayed the same
Both the schema and state stayed the same
questions.explanation: Inserting a record changes the current database state (extension). The schema (intension) describes the database structure and remains unchanged (§2.1.2).

questions.prompt: What does each level of the three-schema architecture describe? Select all that apply.
choices: External schemas describe views for particular user groups
The conceptual schema describes the whole database for a community of users
The internal schema describes physical storage and access paths
The conceptual schema describes only one user group’s external view
questions.explanation: External schemas represent user-group views, the conceptual schema describes the whole community database, and the internal schema covers physical storage and access paths (§2.2.1).

questions.prompt: What is data independence in the three-schema architecture?
choices: Moving every external schema to the internal storage level
Allowing users to change records without satisfying constraints
Keeping a database state unchanged when users make queries
Change one schema level while higher levels remain unchanged
questions.explanation: Data independence is the capacity to change a schema at one level without changing the schema at the next higher level (§2.2.2).

questions.prompt: A DBA adds an access path to speed up course-offering searches while leaving the logical data unchanged. Which kind of data independence does this illustrate?
choices: Physical data independence: change the internal schema
External data independence; a user view was removed
Program-operation independence, because a method implementation changed
Logical data independence, because the conceptual schema changed
questions.explanation: Adding an access structure changes the internal schema; physical data independence allows this without changing the conceptual schema (§2.2.2).

questions.prompt: A conceptual schema is reorganized while user views and their application programs continue to work. What must be adjusted to support this?
choices: All application program definitions
The conceptual-to-external schema mappings
The values in every stored record
The operating system’s disk scheduler
questions.explanation: Logical data independence is supported by changing the relevant view definition and mappings while keeping affected application programs working (§2.2.2).

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a data definition language (DDL)?
choices: Retrieve records one at a time for processing in a host language
Create backup copies of the database on mass storage
Display results in a menu
Define schemas for storage in the catalog
questions.explanation: DDL statements define database schemas; a DDL compiler processes their descriptions and stores them in the catalog (§2.3.1).

questions.prompt: A database request specifies which set of records to retrieve but does not prescribe record-by-record steps. What kind of DML is it?
choices: High-level, nonprocedural DML
A host-language compiler instruction
Low-level procedural DML
A storage definition language
questions.explanation: High-level DML specifies what data to retrieve rather than how to retrieve it, and can operate on sets of records (§2.3.1).

questions.prompt: Which interface guides a user by presenting selectable options instead of requiring query-language syntax?
choices: A DDL compiler
A storage definition language
A menu-based interface
A low-level procedural DML
questions.explanation: Menu-based interfaces guide users through requests by presenting lists of options, so they need not memorize query commands and syntax (§2.3.2).

questions.prompt: Which DBMS components directly support runtime access to stored data? Select all that apply.
choices: Buffering and transaction-management services support runtime data transfer and execution
The DDL compiler chooses the disk search path for each query at runtime
The runtime database processor executes query plans and canned transactions
The stored-data manager controls access to DBMS information on disk
questions.explanation: The runtime processor executes plans and transactions, the stored-data manager accesses disk information, and buffering plus transaction services support execution. The DDL compiler processes schema definitions (§2.4.1).

questions.prompt: Which tasks are handled by common database utilities? Select all that apply.
choices: Loading existing data files into the database
Creating backup copies for recovery
Reorganizing storage and creating access paths
Compile host-language programs into applications
questions.explanation: Common utilities load data, create backups, reorganize storage, and monitor performance. Host-language compilation is part of application program processing (§2.4.2).

questions.prompt: A precompiler extracts embedded DML statements from a host-language program. Which component processes those database statements next?
choices: Stored-data manager next
DDL compiler next
Host-language compiler next
DML compiler processes them next
questions.explanation: The precompiler extracts embedded DML commands and sends them to the DML compiler for compilation (§2.4.1).

questions.prompt: In a centralized DBMS architecture, where are DBMS functions and application processing performed?
choices: On client devices, while the central computer only stores data
On the central computer that houses the DBMS
Across independent database servers, with no central host
On display terminals that contain the complete DBMS
questions.explanation: In the centralized architecture described, all processing, including applications and DBMS functionality, occurs on the computer housing the DBMS (§2.5.1).

questions.prompt: A Web application checks a client’s credentials and applies business rules before sending database requests. Which tier performs that work?
choices: The client presentation tier
The middle application-server tier
The database storage tier that manages persistent files
The external schema level
questions.explanation: The middle tier runs application programs and business rules and can check credentials before forwarding requests to the database server (§2.5.4).

questions.prompt: In a three-tier Web application, which path carries a browser request to stored data and returns results to the user?
choices: Middle-tier application logic → external schema → internal schema → client
Client presentation → database services → application logic → stored data
Database services → client presentation → middle-tier rules → browser
Client → middle tier → database services → client
questions.explanation: The client sends requests to the middle tier, which processes them and issues database requests; results pass back through the middle tier to the client (§2.5.4).

questions.prompt: Which are among the criteria used to classify a DBMS? Select all that apply.
choices: The data model and cost of the DBMS
The number of users the system supports
The number of sites across which the data is distributed
The administrator's display size and resolution
questions.explanation: DBMSs can be classified by data model, number of supported users, distribution across sites, and cost. Display size is not a DBMS classification criterion (§2.6).

questions.prompt: How does a key-value data model organize retrieval?
choices: A hierarchy of records is traversed from a fixed root
A graph edge identifies a document’s storage page
A unique key retrieves its associated value directly by key
A set of tables is searched only by row position
questions.explanation: The key-value model associates a unique key with each value and provides access to the value given its key (§2.6).

questions.prompt: Two sites in a distributed database system use different DBMS software. Which category describes this arrangement?
choices: A single-user DBMS with one database user
A homogeneous DDBMS using matching DBMS software
A centralized DBMS running at one site
A heterogeneous DDBMS
questions.explanation: A heterogeneous distributed DBMS can use different DBMS software at its sites; a homogeneous DDBMS uses the same software (§2.6).
